items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: I had a meeting with Frank Pena and Rosenthal from out of Port Arthur, Texas... Charlie Rosenthal was his name. Very nice man.

ctx.x: Did he treat a lot of people like that? Was he very generous?

Well, he was generous to a lot of people. Frank was a likable individual who just cared for people, and he just liked to get involved. And I was thinking about, I had a meeting with Frank Pena and Rosenthal from out of Port Arthur, Texas. I'm trying to think of Rosenthal. He had a theater and a nightclub, and he used to come here and talk to Frank Pena all the time. Sometimes Frank would send some of his talent over there to Orange, Texas, rather. Charlie Rosenthal was his name. Very nice man. I hope he's still…

Oh, definitely. One point. Earl King told me, he said one of the, the most successful, the recent success of the dew drop wasn't, and the attraction wasn't just the music. He said, but he said a lot, the transvestites and the gay reviews.

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: I highlight, I was talking about Charlie Rosenthal over in Orange, Texas, who was a good friend of Frank Pannier.

ctx.x: So you must have been out all night.

No, I had traveled quite a bit. See, at that time, I was working for a brown, brown, see, that was a liquor company. You know, this old, old Forrester, and early times, and King Liquor at that time. And I used to travel all through Louisiana and part of Texas. If you notice, I have a lot, a lot about Texas in here, about, well, Forrestal, what is the name, Rosenthal out of Orange, Texas, who was a big time promoter. He and Frank Pannier, they were co-promoters on shows from New Orleans all the way over to Orange,…
I'm just curious stuff about Butch Curran, about the traveling, about writing the column and so forth. Go and put your date on it again and put your billboard on it.
